content:
Rumors suggest Apple's fall iPhone lineup this year will center around two models: the iPhone 18 Pro and the iPhone Ultra. Below are the three most important feature differences, excluding price, that may influence your decision to upgrade.

Design: Traditional vs. Foldable

This difference is the most obvious, but worth mentioning, as it is also the most significant distinction.

The iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max will continue the basic design that iPhones have used for years. The screen size and overall appearance are reportedly identical to the previous generation. If you want the feel of a traditional iPhone, the iPhone 18 Pro will be your top choice.

As for the iPhone Ultra, it will be Apple's first foldable phone. Its body design is completely different — the outer screen is shorter and wider than a traditional iPhone, while the inner screen is similar to an iPad mini.

Camera: Pro Models Still Reign Supreme

Apple has always reserved its most cutting-edge and innovative camera technology for the Pro models. This year looks set to continue that tradition.

The iPhone Ultra's camera specs are expected to be largely the same as the iPhone 18 Pro's, but with one major exception: it will not include a telephoto lens.

Rumor has it that the iPhone Ultra will carry the same main lens, ultrawide lens, and front-facing camera as the Pro lineup. However, the telephoto lens will remain exclusive to the Pro models, with performance expected to reach new heights this year.

Performance: Both Feature the A20 Pro Chip, but Materials Affect Performance

Both the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Ultra are expected to run on the A20 Pro chip. However, due to differences in design and materials, performance may vary.

The iPhone 18 Pro will carry forward the unibody aluminum design introduced with the iPhone 17 Pro, along with a vapor chamber for cooling. These two changes made the iPhone 17 Pro's overall performance better than its predecessor, as the phone can stay cooler under heavy workloads.

The iPhone Ultra will adopt a slim, lightweight titanium design similar to the iPhone Air. It may also feature a vapor chamber, but only one leaker has made this claim so far. However, due to the different materials, even though the iPhone Ultra and iPhone 18 Pro use the same chip, performance may be slightly inferior under direct sunlight or intense use.
